clue.text: American woman's talk is a cutting thing

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman, and the 's adds an S
word, as in 'have a word', means a talk

explanation.surface: An American woman's speech is described as cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: BROAD is dated American slang for a woman; the possessive supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy sword with a wide blade is a weapon that cuts.

clue.text: Observe, evenly, fourth of July gathering

indicators.note: evenly asks for the letters in the even-numbered places of the word Observe
fourth of asks for the letter in fourth place of the word July

explanation.surface: Watching a crowd assemble on the Fourth of July, Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of Observe, B, E, V; 'fourth of' takes the fourth letter of July, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group or flock, especially of quails or of people.

clue.text: Dutiful old boy's retainer

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a retainer is a household servant

explanation.surface: A former pupil's faithful household servant is dutiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone observant keeps the rules and customs carefully, as in religiously observant.

clue.text: Worn out from early morning run in…

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for run is placed inside the word for early morning

parts.note: dawn is the early morning
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Feeling exhausted after an early morning jog.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next two, all defined by 'worn out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn face looks tired and haggard from strain.

clue.text: …more worn out clothes? That's right…

parts.note: wear means clothing, as in menswear
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: Asking whether clothes are more threadbare, and agreeing they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearier is the comparative of weary, which means tired or exhausted.

clue.text: …about worn out — went to bed

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
tired means worn out

explanation.surface: Being exhausted, someone turned in for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to go to bed for the night.

clue.text: Due to be married — just after ring

indicators.note: just after places the word for be married following the letter for ring

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
to wed is to be married

explanation.surface: A couple about to marry immediately after exchanging rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owed is money due to someone, an outstanding debt.

clue.text: Shudder! It's topless hag!

indicators.note: topless says the word for shudder loses its first letter, its top in a down entry

parts.note: a twitch is a sudden shudder or jerk

explanation.surface: A shocked cry at seeing a topless old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hag is an ugly old woman, traditionally a sorceress.

clue.text: Prize for painting?

definitions.meaning: a medal or honour awarded to someone
the act of painting and papering a room

explanation.definitionFit: A decoration is both a medal awarded as an honour and the adornment of a room with paint.

clue.text: Sort of rum made with rare ingredients

indicators.note: ingredients suggests the letters of the words made and rare are mixed together

explanation.surface: A rum produced using unusual components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredients' signals mixing the letters of MADE and RARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara rum comes from Guyana, named after the Demerara river region.

clue.text: Landscape is turner's first in London museum

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the abbreviation for the London museum

parts.note: V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
taken as written

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word turner's

explanation.surface: A J.M.W. Turner landscape displayed as the highlight of a London gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital-less 'turner' tempts you to think of the painter; only its first letter T is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a pleasing view, as of scenery.

clue.text: Genuine gold article found on northern jerk

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the is the definite article
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: Real gold jewellery found on a northern idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic and genuine are synonyms: real, not fake.

clue.text: More stylish row has split inside

indicators.note: inside places the word for split within the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
to rend is to split or tear

explanation.surface: A fashionable quarrel has divided people inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendier is the comparative of trendy, meaning fashionable.

clue.text: Number three, possibly

definitions.note: read as numb-er, something that numbs

indicators.note: possibly suggests the word three could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Guessing that a certain digit is three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but numb-er, an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic, a substance that deadens feeling.

clue.text: Rat I uncovered with queens hussar?

indicators.note: uncovered suggests the letters of rat, I and queens are laid open and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exposes a rat in the company of queens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' signals rearranging RAT I QUEENS; the question mark marks hussar as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalry soldier, so an example of a horseman.

clue.text: Classy graffiti, some say, in queens district

indicators.note: in places the classy and graffiti pieces within the two queens

parts.note: Q is an abbreviation for queen
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a queen's royal cipher
U means upper-class
some people regard graffiti as art

explanation.surface: Stylish street art in the New York borough of Queens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' does not signal a sound-alike here: it hedges the claim that graffiti counts as street art. 'queens' supplies two royal abbreviations at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter is a district of a town, such as the Latin Quarter.

clue.text: Fall wearing irregular rose glasses

indicators.note: wearing in a down clue puts the word for fall on top of the next piece

parts.note: to tumble is to fall

indicators.note: irregular asks for alternate letters of the word rose

explanation.surface: Someone tumbling while wearing odd rose-tinted spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' takes R and S, the alternate letters of ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumblers are flat-bottomed drinking vessels.

clue.text: Frank, candid writer, perhaps

definitions.meaning: Anne Frank, famous for her wartime journal
someone who writes frankly in a private journal

explanation.definitionFit: Anne Frank kept a famous journal, and a journal keeper writes candid daily entries.

clue.text: Kind of tense and below par

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense describing ongoing past action

explanation.definitionFit: Imperfect names a past tense in grammar and also means flawed or not up to scratch.

clue.text: Puts under carved stone holding bits of information

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged letters contain the abbreviation for bits of information
carved suggests the letters of stone are cut into a new shape

parts.note: MB is megabytes, units of computer data

explanation.surface: A carved gravestone bearing some details puts someone underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carved' rearranges the five letters to ENTOS before the computing units go inside; 'Puts under' means buries, not sedates.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to bury, placing someone in the ground.

clue.text: Labour leader gripped by brutal scrap

indicators.note: gripped by places the leader's letter inside the word for brutal

parts.note: savage means brutal

indicators.note: leader asks for the first letter of the word Labour

explanation.surface: The Labour Party leader caught up in a vicious fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the UK's main left-wing party; 'scrap' looks like a fight but means rescued waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is material rescued from waste, such as scrap metal.

clue.text: Treatment for bad state of shock?

definitions.text: Treatment for bad state of shock?

parts.words: Treatment for bad state of shock?
parts.note: a shock here is a thick mass of hair, not a trauma, so the treatment is a hair wash

explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a washing treatment for hair, and a shock of hair is a mop of it.

clue.text: It's somehow nicer in the home counties — honest

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the abbreviation for the home counties

parts.note: SE, south-east England, is where the home counties lie

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of nicer arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: People are somehow pleasanter in the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are those surrounding London, in south-east England (SE).
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere and honest both mean genuine and without deceit.

clue.text: Place to reserve a place in the sun?

definitions.text: Place to reserve a place in the sun?

parts.words: Place to reserve a place in the sun?
parts.note: holidaymakers drape a beach cloth over a sunlounger to claim it early

explanation.definitionFit: Tourists famously lay a bath sheet on a poolside lounger to reserve it.

clue.text: Thin piece of iron held in battle

indicators.note: held in places the symbol for iron inside the word for battle

parts.note: war is battle
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A slender piece of iron carried into combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer is a very thin slice or biscuit.

clue.text: You may get a punch from him!

definitions.text: You may get a punch from him!

parts.words: You may get a punch from him!
parts.note: punch is a mixed drink served at a pub, not a blow

explanation.definitionFit: A publican serves drinks, including bowls of punch.

clue.text: Drink up — it's grand

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for grand is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: regal means grand or majestic

explanation.surface: A toast: drink up, it's splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a pale beer, a common alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Endless work for the boss

indicators.note: endless says the word for work loses its final letter

parts.note: to study is to work at learning

explanation.surface: Ceaseless toil on behalf of the employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is not an employer but a raised knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is an ornamental knob or projection, as a stud is.

clue.text: Enrage? True, if in a rage

indicators.note: rage suggests the letters of true, if, in, a are thrown about wildly

explanation.surface: Agreeing that someone in a fury is enraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' are part of the fodder, not a link; 'rage' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To infuriate is to make someone furious, synonymous with to enrage.

clue.text: Mince sounds fantastic

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word for mince is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to grate food is to shred or mince it

explanation.surface: Minced meat is said to be wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Great and fantastic are both terms of strong approval.

clue.text: Average in Latin or maths

indicators.note: in signals the letters are found inside the words Latin or maths

explanation.surface: Typical school subjects, Latin or maths.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual or average standard.

clue.text: Famous, unusual beetle car — Disney's first

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters of beetle and car are made to look different
first asks for the opening letter of the word Disney's

explanation.surface: A celebrated Disney film about an odd Volkswagen Beetle car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns BEETLE CAR into CELEBRATE; Disney's Herbie films starred a VW Beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated means renowned or widely acclaimed.
